subsections.title: Government
subsections.content: São Tomé and Príncipe operates a presidential-parliamentary democracy. The President is elected for two 5-year terms, while the Prime Minister holds most executive powers. Governments are often unstable due to coalition systems, and institutions face challenges from corruption and limited efficiency.

subsections.title: Trade
subsections.content: The country is not a WTO member, limiting global trade integration. Trade is heavily dependent on Europe, especially Portugal. Imports significantly exceed exports, creating a large trade deficit and reliance on external goods.

subsections.title: Tax Policies
subsections.content: The tax system includes a 10% VAT and progressive income tax up to 25%. Although structured, enforcement is weak due to administrative limitations and a large informal sector.

subsections.title: Political Issues
subsections.content: Key issues include weak transparency, corruption, limited media independence, and difficulties accessing public information. Enforcement of labor laws and regulations remains weak.

subsections.title: Political Trends
subsections.content: The country has a stable democratic system with peaceful transitions of power. However, institutional weaknesses and political fragmentation continue to affect governance.

subsections.title: Inflation
subsections.content: Inflation is relatively high but declining, reaching around 9–10% in 2026. Historically, it has been volatile, affecting purchasing power.

subsections.title: Interest Rate
subsections.content: Interest rates average around 10%, reflecting inflation control policies. High rates limit borrowing and private investment.

subsections.title: Exchange Rate
subsections.content: The local currency is pegged to the euro, which stabilizes prices but limits monetary flexibility and increases dependence on foreign reserves.

subsections.title: Economic Growth
subsections.content: Growth is modest (~1.7%), with heavy reliance on agriculture, tourism, and foreign aid. The economy is vulnerable to external shocks.

subsections.title: Unemployment
subsections.content: Unemployment is around 9–10%, but a large informal sector dominates employment, reducing job security and productivity.

subsections.title: Demographics
subsections.content: Population is حوالي 247,000 with steady growth. The country has a young population and high dependency on working-age individuals.

subsections.title: Lifestyle
subsections.content: The culture follows a 'Leve Leve' relaxed lifestyle focused on community and simplicity, influenced by African and Portuguese traditions.

subsections.title: Education
subsections.content: Primary enrollment is high and literacy rates are improving, but challenges remain in quality and secondary education completion.

subsections.title: Consumer Behavior
subsections.content: Consumers focus on essential goods due to limited income. Informal markets dominate, and the country relies heavily on imported products.

subsections.title: Healthcare
subsections.content: Healthcare infrastructure is limited. There is only one major hospital, and advanced treatment often requires travel abroad.

subsections.title: Education Technology
subsections.content: Technology use in schools is limited but improving through international programs and digital learning initiatives.

subsections.title: Challenges
subsections.content: Challenges include weak infrastructure, limited internet access, lack of devices, and insufficient teacher training.

subsections.title: Digital Adoption
subsections.content: Mobile penetration is growing (~60%+). Internet usage is increasing but uneven, especially between urban and rural areas.

subsections.title: Overview
subsections.content: The country is vulnerable to climate change due to its small island geography.

subsections.title: Climate Risks
subsections.content: Key risks include floods, coastal erosion, and sea-level rise that impact agriculture and infrastructure.

subsections.title: Response
subsections.content: Government and international organizations are implementing environmental protection and climate resilience projects.

subsections.title: Legal System
subsections.content: The legal system is based on Portuguese law and includes constitutional and judicial courts.

subsections.title: Investment Laws
subsections.content: Foreign investment is allowed with incentives and protections against expropriation.

subsections.title: Land Access
subsections.content: Most land is government-owned and accessed through concessions rather than ownership.

subsections.title: Labor Laws
subsections.content: Labor laws exist but enforcement is weak. Foreign workers require permits.
